note: Countries whose surname data was sought and not obtained, with what was actually tried. A gap somebody can see is worth more than a gap they cannot, and without this file the next person spends the same afternoon finding the same three walls. A «not found» verdict is weaker than a «refused» one: it means this project looked and did not find, not that the data is absent. Both are worth writing down and they are not the same claim. Five of the eight were re-tested on 21 September 2026 against live endpoints rather than remembered ones, and every refusal held — but three of them are now evidence where they were inference. Croatia's statistics API works and has no surname table; Denmark's entire table list contains no name table; Sweden lists two name folders it will not serve. Finland's holder answers 403 to a crawler and this atlas does not climb bot gates, so that one is refused by choice as much as by circumstance. The Netherlands needs a letter to the Meertens Instituut, which is not a thing a script can send.

refused.name: Belgium
tried: statbel.fgov.be/en/open-data — the full open-data catalogue searched for name/nom/naam
refused.why: Statbel publishes first names in detail — by year, region and sex — and no surname dataset at all. The gap is in what Belgium chooses to publish, not in what it holds.

refused.name: Czechia
tried: mvcr.cz/clanek/cetnost-jmen-a-prijmeni.aspx — the page loads and is headed «Archiv», with no file of any kind left on it
no surname table in the Czech Statistical Office's own catalogue
mvcr.cz/clanek/cetnost-jmen-a-prijmeni — followed the redirect to mv.gov.cz, which 404s
refused.verdict: the page has moved and then gone
refused.why: RETRIED 21 September. The old Ministry of the Interior URL now redirects to mv.gov.cz and returns 404 there. The frequency service that used to publish this is gone rather than relocated.

refused.name: Denmark
tried: api.statbank.dk — all 2,308 tables listed and searched for navn/fornavn/efternavn: none
dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/borgere/navne — the page exists and offers «hvor mange hedder», an interactive lookup for one name at a time
api.statbank.dk/v1/tables — the COMPLETE table list, 531 KB, searched for 'navn'
refused.verdict: zero name tables in the whole bank
refused.why: RETRIED 21 September. The refusal said Statistics Denmark 'does not put names in its statistics bank at all', which was inference from a failed lookup. The entire table list has now been downloaded and searched: not one of its tables mentions navn. The inference was right and is now evidence.

refused.name: Finland
tried: pxdata.stat.fi StatFin — all 135 subject folders, none name-related
avoindata.fi — HTTP 403 to every request
avoindata.fi CKAN — 403 to an identified crawler
pxdata.stat.fi PxWeb — answers, and holds no names
refused.verdict: the holder gates crawlers, and the statistics office has no names
refused.why: RETRIED 21 September. Statistics Finland's PxWeb works and has no name data, which is consistent: the names belong to the DVV. The DVV's dataset sits on avoindata.fi, which answers 403 to an identified crawler. THIS ATLAS DOES NOT CLIMB BOT GATES — the same rule that keeps it off the Antenati portal and IrishGenealogy — so this stays refused until a human downloads it or the gate lifts.

refused.name: Croatia
tried: podaci.dzs.hr CKAN package_search for «prezimena» — no parseable response
data.gov.hr CKAN package_search for «prezimena» — answers 200 but not JSON
podaci.dzs.hr CKAN — 404
opendata.dzs.hr — no answer
web.dzs.hr/PXWeb/api/v1 — the whole PxWeb tree walked two levels deep, looking for ime/prezime/name in every folder
refused.verdict: the API answers now, and holds no names
refused.why: RETRIED 21 September and the verdict is firmer, not weaker. The refusal said the open-data portal 'responds but not to a CKAN search', which left open the possibility that the data existed behind a working endpoint. The DZS PxWeb API does work — 20 subject folders, navigable — and walking it finds no surname table at all. The one name-shaped hit was 'Eksperimentalne statistike' under Tourism, matching on the letters in 'eksperimentalne'. Croatia is this atlas's deepest ground and has no published surname counts; that is now a checked fact rather than a failed search.

refused.name: Italy
tried: esploradati.istat.it SDMX dataflow list — no parseable response to a documented Accept header
istat.it — responds, but publishes no surname frequency series that this probe could find
refused.why: ISTAT does not appear to publish surname frequencies. What circulates for Italy is derived from telephone directories by commercial sites, which is neither open nor redistributable. Recorded as NOT FOUND rather than as absent — a human who knows ISTAT may know better, and this is three archives' core ground.

refused.name: Netherlands
tried: opendata.cbs.nl catalogue search — no surname table
cbgfamilienamen.nl (Meertens familienamenbank) — HTTP 403
refused.why: CBS publishes no surname frequencies. The real Dutch source is the Meertens Nederlandse Familienamenbank, which is a research database rather than open government data. This one should be asked for rather than taken.

refused.name: Sweden
tried: api.scb.se BE0001 «Namnstatistik» — the folder is listed and its two sub-folders, BE0001D and BE0001G, both answer 400 Bad Request
api.scb.se/OV0104/v1/doris/en/ssd/BE/BE0001 — the two name folders found, then opened
refused.verdict: the folders are listed and cannot be entered
refused.why: RETRIED 21 September. Both folders are still advertised in the tree — 'Newborn' and 'All registered persons in Sweden', each marked 'Old tables not updated' — and every path inside them answers 400. SCB lists what it no longer serves, which is why this looked available and is not.
